messages:
olivia: quick summary from the 0200 canary — we saw a bunch of short-lived p99 spikes when kernel fallback happened under bursty arrival. thinking about an adaptive safety-margin instead of our static 75% util target. it nudges target lower when kernel-switch cost + kvcache-miss tail risk is high.

mike: can you drop the raw numbers?

olivia: yup, paste from the profiler + tail sampler: 
```
model: llama-13b-q4
seq: 256
kernels: fused-attn (A) vs fallback (B)
A: avg_tok_ms=0.92  p95=1.9  p99=4.8
B: avg_tok_ms=1.35  p95=2.6  p99=9.1
kv miss_rate=11.8%  (first-requests + cold sessions) -> add about +1.1ms median, +3.2ms tail
gpu util observed: nominal 78% -> bursts hit 92-96% during microburst sets
kernel-switch penalty (A->B): ~2.7ms extra on first token after switch
```

jordan: oof that A->B penalty explains the p99 jump. are these single-host numbers or multi-host?

olivia: single host, dedicated 8xA100. same shape in multi-host but amplified when kvcache misses align across replicas.

anya: what's the proposed adaptive rule? per-model windowed telemetry?

olivia: proposal: compute a per-model safety_margin S = base(75%) + w1*recent_kernel_switch_rate + w2*kv_miss_tail_factor + w3*p99_surge_score. S clipped [55,90]. admission uses target_util = 100 - S. admission controller then applies soft-admit (queue) if queue latency budget < X else soft-shed.

mike: how do we get those weights? want simplicity: maybe two tiers (low/med/high risk) instead of continuous weights.

jordan: agree on tiers. low: <3% switch rate & kv_miss<5% -> target 84%. med: default 75%. high: target 65%.

olivia: tested both. continuous version gave slightly better throughput (~2.5% uplift) for same p99, but tiers are way simpler.

ci-bot: loadtest results uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/run/2945 (summary attached) :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: summary: baseline (static75) p99=9.1ms  throughput=100k toks/s; adaptive-tier p99=5.3ms throughput=96.8k toks/s; continuous-adaptive p99=5.0ms throughput=98.5k toks/s

anya: so ~3-5% throughput loss vs baseline but p99 cut by ~45%. that seems acceptable for most customers.

sre-jen: need playbook changes: alert when margin bumps >10% within 5m and auto-unwind canary flag. also add runbook steps for rollback if error rates spike.

mike: microbatch sizing — did we change batch windows? because smaller microbatches reduce kernel switch sync but hurt throughput.

olivia: we kept microbatch policy unchanged in these runs. separate experiment: shrinking max microbatch by 20% reduced p99 by ~0.6ms but dropped throughput more (~4%). combined with adaptive margin it was marginally better for tail but not worth ops complexity.

jordan: important bit: admission should be kernel-aware. if we detect a chain of requests likely to cause a switch (e.g., longer sequence or KV-miss pattern), we should prefer queuing until kernel warms. otherwise we flip fast.

anya: can we add a lightweight probe when deciding admit: peek at request seq_len + kvcache-hit-estimate and if risk_score>threshold, increase margin locally?

olivia: yes, implemented a POC: risk_score = 0.6*is_long_seq + 0.4*kvcache_prob. felt cheap.

ci-bot: stress test (90th percentile traffic pattern) logs: 
```
-- event at t=120s --
burst of 2k reqs/s for 18s, kernel-switch rate up 4.2%
static75: p99 spikes to 22ms and 1 host hit gpu OOM throttle (recovered)
adaptive-tier: p99 peak 7.4ms, no OOMs, sustained throughput -3.1%
```

mike: any regressions in memory or QPS fairness?
olivia: no mem regressions. fairness: a tiny increase in request queuing for high-risk sessions, but fairness across tenants unchanged.

jordan: ops question: how do we surface this in Console? need per-model "safety margin" metric and a heatmap of kernel-switch costs.

anya: and add a probe for KV-cache miss alignment across replicas. when misses align we should be extra conservative.

sre-jen: please add an alert threshold for aligned-kv-miss (e.g., >8% across >30% hosts) -> auto-escalate.

olivia: next steps: (1) narrow to tiered adaptive config for canary rollout (flag: adaptive_headroom_tiered=true) (2) add console metrics + alert hooks (3) small tweak to admission: kernel-aware peek risk (POC) (4) 48h canary on dedicated cluster + rollback on alerts.

mike: SGTM. make the config defaults conservative. can we gate by plan (only enterprise + internal clusters for now)?

olivia: yeah internal + enterprise for the first week. will open PR with config + canary yaml.

jordan: add a short note about the kernel-switch measurement methodology to the PR so reviewers can sanity-check.

olivia: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
